ClamStop help

Closing the lid

In the settings, General tab, “When I close the lid” chooses between sleep, even with a screen plugged in, and what macOS does on its own. “Hibernate” sets how long the Mac sleeps before it saves its memory to disk and stops using the battery.

Background service

ClamStop needs its background service, approved once in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions (Login Items on macOS 14): turn the ClamStop switch on and authenticate.

If the switch is on and ClamStop still waits, click Reinstall Background Service in the settings, then turn the switch on once if macOS asks.

Staying awake

“Stay Awake” in the menu, rules, AI agents and chosen apps can keep the Mac awake with the lid closed, within the limits of the Safety tab. By default this only works on the power adapter.

The Mac does not sleep, or sleeps too soon

What Keeps My Mac Awake… in the menu lists what stops the Mac from sleeping on its own. The sleep journal, in the Diagnostics tab, shows when it slept, woke and why. ClamStop works only while the app runs.

Health check and problem reports

The Diagnostics tab checks what could stop ClamStop from working and says what to do. To report a problem, use Report on GitHub… or Report by Email… there: you read the report before sending it.

Uninstall

  1. Open the ClamStop settings (menu bar icon > Settings…, or open the app again from the Applications folder).
  2. Click Uninstall ClamStop…, then Uninstall. The default sleep settings are restored and the background service is removed.
  3. Move ClamStop from the Applications folder to the Trash.

No cookies, no trackers.
